text:
{{Short description|43rd season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1973–74 National Hurling League |image = |dates =7 October 1973 – 5 May 1974 |teams = |team1 = Cork |captain1 = [[John Horgan (hurler)|John Horgan]] |manager1 = |titles = 10th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two= |previous = [[1972–73 National Hurling League|1972–73]] |next = [[1974–75 National Hurling League|1974–75]] }} The '''1973–74 National Hurling League''' was the 43rd season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1973-74 |winners=[[Cork GAA|Cork]]
10th National League title
Captain: [[John Horgan (hurler)|John Horgan]]
Manager: [[Willie John Daly]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer=[[File: Colours of Dublin.svg|border|20px]] [[Pat Quigley]] (2-49) |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= 60 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1972-73 National Hurling League|1972-73]] |nextseason=[[1974-75 National Hurling League|1974-75]] |updated=12 March 2017 }} [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1972-73 National Hurling League|1972-73 season]]. On 5 May 1974, [[Cork GAA|Cork]] won the title following a 6–15 to 1–12 win over [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the final. It was their 10th league title overall and their first since [[1971-72 National Hurling League|1971-72]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} Dublin's [[Pat Quigley]] was the Division 1 top scorer with 2-49. ===Division 1A table=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: centre;" !width=20|Pos !width=150|Team !width=20|Pld !width=20|W !width=20|D !width=20|L !width=20|Diff !width=20|Pts !width=250|Notes |- style="background:gold;" |'''1'''||align=left|''' [[Cork GAA|Cork]] '''||'''7'''||'''5'''||'''1'''||'''1'''||'''+28'''||'''11'''|| Division 1 champions |- style="background:silver;" |'''2'''||align=left|''' [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] '''||'''7'''||'''4'''||'''2'''||'''1'''||'''+30'''||'''10'''|| Division 1 runners-up |- style |'''3'''||align=left|''' [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] '''||'''7'''||'''4'''||'''0'''||'''3'''||'''+10'''||'''8''' |- style |'''4'''||align=left|''' [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] '''||'''7'''||'''3'''||'''1'''||'''3'''||'''+3'''||'''7''' |- style |'''5'''||align=left|''' [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] '''||'''7'''||'''3'''||'''0'''||'''4'''||'''-2'''||'''6''' |- style |'''6'''||align=left|''' [[Clare GAA|Clare]] '''||'''7'''||'''3'''||'''0'''||'''4'''||'''-13'''||'''6''' |- style |'''7'''||align=left|''' [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] '''||'''7'''||'''1'''||'''2'''||'''4'''||'''-6'''||'''4''' |- style="background:#FFC0CB;" |'''8'''||align=left|''' [[Galway GAA|Galway]] '''||'''7'''||'''2'''||'''0'''||'''5'''||'''-50'''||'''4'''|| Relegated to Division 1B |} ===Group stage=== {{football box collapsible |date = 7 October 1973 |team1 = [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] |score = 1-14 -
